beats.text: Two students come to Confucius. One has read everything. One only sits and thinks.
He warns them both, because each has fallen into a different trap.
"Learning without thought is labour lost; thought without learning is perilous."
Pile up facts you never question, and you carry a library you cannot use.
But spin ideas with nothing to test them against, and you drift into clever nonsense.
Wisdom lives in the loop between them — study, reflect, study again.
Don't just collect knowledge. Don't just daydream. Do both, in turn, for life.

source_note: Quote: Analects II.15, trans. James Legge (public domain).
